response.consequence: For up to 60 seconds after an allowlist change, queries return the wrong count semantics. Raw count() is returned where upsampled_count() is expected, or the reverse. response.explanation: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches the eligibility result for 60s under a key built from the organization id and hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined, but a grep of the snapshot finds no caller. The code that updates `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` therefore never clears the entry. The invalidator also couldn't clear entries reliably. Each distinct project subset has its own key, and the invalidator only deletes the one key for the exact subset it is given. After an allowlist change, any query whose project set was cached before the change keeps its old answer for up to 60s. A project that was added is still treated as not upsampled, and one that was removed is still upsampled. The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says the config is read fresh so the latest state is always used. The cache layer in front of it defeats that. Using hash() on the tuple also adds a needless collision risk, because two different project sets could share a key. A joined string of the sorted ids would avoid that.
response.title: Cached allowlist eligibility is never invalidated when the allowlist changes

Also the cached boolean is reused across requests with different datasets and queries (the dataset check is applied after the cache lookup, so this part is fine). Collisions between different project sets could return wrong eligibility and wrongly upsample counts.
